goal_complete-mscs-seattle-prerequisite-.title: Complete MSCS Seattle prerequisite graph
goal_complete-mscs-seattle-prerequisite-.description: The Prerequisite Graph must show every course listed on the official MSCS Seattle program requirements page, including courses with no parsed prerequisites, plus only the cataloged external prerequisites those courses actually reference.

goal_graph-line-focus-details-and-plan-f.title: Graph line-focus, details, and plan-from-line
goal_graph-line-focus-details-and-plan-f.description: Users can leave a selected graph line and return to the current map, see the clicked course in the inspector, and add that line's catalog courses to a semester.

goal_double-click-course-connections-esc.title: Double-click course connections, Escape back
goal_double-click-course-connections-esc.description: Double-clicking a course card enters that course's connections view. Escape restores the previous map view, including Entire program.

goal_seat-unlock-targets-beside-their-so.title: Seat unlock targets beside their sources
goal_seat-unlock-targets-beside-their-so.description: Program map courses sit next to the courses that unlock them. A two-source target such as CS 6220 stays in that source band. A target with five or more sources sits on the median source row so the bus can surround those courses and point in.

ticket-show-the-full-mscs-seattle-prereq.title: Show the full MSCS Seattle prerequisite graph
ticket-show-the-full-mscs-seattle-prereq.brief: Default Prerequisite Graph must render every official MSCS Seattle program course from the catalog page, including isolated courses with no prerequisites. Keep neighborhood zoom. Do not invent offerings. Restrict the published catalog graph to program courses plus their requirement closure so undergraduate bulk listings stop hiding the program.
acceptance: Opening /map without changing filters shows every core, breadth, and elective course listed on the official MSCS Seattle program requirements page as a node, including CS 5800 and CS 5100 which have no parsed prerequisites.
Direct external prerequisites of those program courses, such as CS 5004 for CS 5500, remain visible. Unrelated undergraduate CS listings such as CS 1800 are not in the published catalog snapshot.
The Show control still offers Immediate neighborhood and that view of CS 5500 stays a local neighborhood rather than replacing the entire-program default.
Grade floors such as C- parse as minimumGrade C- rather than an unknown hyphen token; npm test and npm run typecheck pass.

ticket-lay-out-the-program-map-as-a-prer.title: Lay out the program map as a prerequisite flow
ticket-lay-out-the-program-map-as-a-prer.brief: Default Prerequisite Graph should place cataloged prerequisites to the left of the courses they unlock, and inspector code chips should pan the camera to that course instead of only opening a dialog.
acceptance: On the default entire-program map, CS 5004 and CS 5010 sit to the left of CS 5500, and CS 5500 sits to the left of CS 6510.
Courses with no parsed arrows remain on the map packed below the connected flow; CS 5800 and CS 5100 are still present.
Clicking a prerequisite or unlock chip in the map inspector selects that course and pans to it when it is on the current view; a chip for a course not on this view opens that course neighborhood.
Immediate neighborhood of CS 5500 stays the local four-course set; npm test and npm run typecheck pass.

ticket-show-titles-and-real-prerequisite.title: Show titles and real prerequisite arrows
ticket-show-titles-and-real-prerequisite.brief: Entire-program map should keep course titles, draw arrows only for the selected course's parsed prerequisite chain, and sit a sole prerequisite immediately left of the course that names it.
acceptance: Entire-program map nodes show the course title, not only the code.
Unrelated neighbors are not visually linked: the entire-program map draws arrows only for the selected course's parsed prerequisite and unlock chain.
A course that is the sole on-map prerequisite of another sits immediately left of it on the same row, with the arrow pointing at that course.
Selecting PHYS 5116 shows only the arrow to CS 7332 and explains that CS 7332 named this external code; npm test and npm run typecheck pass.

ticket-add-ctrl-f-find-on-the-prerequisi.title: Add Ctrl+F find on the prerequisite map
ticket-add-ctrl-f-find-on-the-prerequisi.brief: Browser Ctrl+F cannot find off-screen React Flow nodes. The map needs an in-page find that focuses with Ctrl+F and jumps through matching courses.
acceptance: On /map, Ctrl+F or Cmd+F focuses the graph find field and does not open the browser find bar.
Typing a course code or title lists matches; Enter or F3 jumps to the next match and pans if it is on the current view.
A query such as cs5500 or PHYS 5116 locates that course even when the node is off-screen; Escape clears the find field.
npm test and npm run typecheck pass.

ticket-seat-coreq-partners-beside-their-.title: Seat coreq partners beside their course and reuse skill-tree neighborhood layout
ticket-seat-coreq-partners-beside-their-.brief: Finish skill-tree leftovers: CS 5011 must sit on the next row under CS 5010, and neighborhood/depth views must use layoutProgramFlow instead of wrap-4 packing.
acceptance: On the Seattle program map, CS 5011.x equals CS 5010.x and CS 5011.y equals CS 5010.y plus PROGRAM_ROW; a synthetic exclusive coreq pair with no outgoing unlocks also occupies consecutive rows in the same column.

Show neighborhood of CS 5500 still contains exactly CS 5004, CS 5010, CS 5500, CS 6510; those four lay out left-to-right as a skill tree (5004 and 5010 left of 5500, 5500 left of 6510). GraphWorkspace depth views other than program call layoutProgramFlow and no longer use wrap=4 packing.
npm test and npm run typecheck both exit 0.

ticket-clear-remaining-map-leftovers-bef.title: Clear remaining map leftovers before closing the MSCS graph goal
ticket-clear-remaining-map-leftovers-bef.brief: Batch-fix named leftover debt: compact eligible pill clipping, course-details dialog stealing Ctrl+F, and Escape not clearing map find after a canvas click.
acceptance: Compact graph course cards show the eligible status in full with no CSS ellipsis clipping; the inspector may keep the long Prerequisite eligible wording.
Map Ctrl+F is skipped while a native course-details dialog is open (closest dialog or role=dialog). The Modal dialog is discoverable as a dialog to that skip.
Escape clears the graph find field when it has text even if the React Flow canvas is focused; Escape inside an open dialog does not get stolen by map find.
npm test and npm run typecheck both exit 0.

ticket-exit-line-focus-show-course-detai.title: Exit line-focus, show course details, add line to plan
ticket-exit-line-focus-show-course-detai.brief: After selecting a colored graph line, users can return to the current map, see the clicked course in the inspector, and add that line's catalog courses to a chosen semester without changing map scope.
acceptance: With a relationship selected, a visible Exit line focus control, Escape from the graph layout (including the inspector), and a click on empty map all clear the selection and restore the previous map scope and zoom; they do not switch depth to This course's full chain.

Clicking a course card updates the inspector heading, title, credits, and description for that course even while a line is selected; it does not require Full course details. Dimmed cards remain clickable.

With a line selected, Add this line to a semester lists the line's program courses, skips externals and already-recorded codes, and addCourse-equivalent inserts the rest into the chosen term without exceeding 32 courses; npm test and npm run typecheck pass.

ticket-double-click-enters-course-connec.title: Double-click enters course connections; Escape restores previous view
ticket-double-click-enters-course-connec.brief: Double-clicking a course card (or table course) switches the map to This course's connections for that code and remembers the prior scope. Escape restores that prior view after find-clear and line-focus, including Entire program.
acceptance: Double-clicking a course while Entire program (or another scope) is showing enters GraphScope 1 for that course, focuses it, and records the previous depth/focus/zoom.

Escape from the graph layout restores the recorded previous view; a second drill-in stacks so Escape returns one level at a time. Escape still clears find text first, then line focus, and does not steal dialogs, selects, or fullscreen.

Double-clicking a course already shown as This course's connections does not push a duplicate view. Explicit Show dropdown, locate/search focus, and Show entire program start a new destination and clear the drill-in stack.
npm test and npm run typecheck pass.

ticket-place-unlock-targets-beside-sourc.title: Place unlock targets beside sources and center high fan-in
ticket-place-unlock-targets-beside-sourc.brief: Stop parking CS 6220 far from CS 5800 and CS 7800. Place each unlocked course at the median row of its on-map sources. Cluster those sources. Adjacent-column arrows use a short surround-then-point bus. Five or more sources keep the target in the middle of that vertical span.
acceptance: On the entire-program layout, CS 6220 sits to the right of CS 5800 and CS 7800, its y is between those two source rows, and those two sources occupy consecutive rows.
A synthetic course with five same-column sources sits on the median source row, and those sources occupy five consecutive rows so the bus can surround them.
Sole-prerequisite pairs still share a row; CS 5004 and CS 5010 stay left of CS 5500; npm test and npm run typecheck pass.
